data.label: Maintenance records
data.description: Existing synthetic maintenance and failure history. These records are the label source.

data.label: Event Hubs ingestion
data.description: Receives sensor events and captures them to the data lake.

data.label: Data lake
data.description: Private storage for raw telemetry, maintenance records and features. Records are loaded in batch.

data.label: Feature preparation
data.description: Builds windowed sensor features and joins them with time-aligned failure labels.

data.label: Training + held-out eval
data.description: Trains on earlier periods and evaluates on a later held-out period. Reports precision, recall and false alarms.

data.label: Model registry
data.description: Holds versioned models together with their evaluation evidence. Only approved versions are promoted.

data.label: Batch scoring
data.description: Scores recent features with the promoted model version and outputs a risk for each asset.

data.label: Drift monitoring
data.description: Compares input and prediction drift with the training baseline and alerts the model owner.
data.service: Azure Machine Learning model monitoring + Azure Monitor

data.label: Work-order draft
data.description: Turns high-risk scores into draft work orders. These are drafts only; it has no equipment-control path.

data.label: Maintenance operator
data.description: Reviews, approves or rejects the drafts.

brief.application: Use Azure for this synthetic architecture qualification. Predict equipment maintenance needs from synthetic sensor histories and maintenance records. Include ingestion, feature preparation, a versioned prediction model, held-out evaluation, drift monitoring and an operator work-order draft. No automatic equipment control. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: How much history do you have for what you want to predict?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “three years of sales by store” or “failure records since 2020”.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the Predictive ML design.

requirements.statement: Proposed: predictions only create draft work orders that an operator approves. The system never sends commands to equipment.
requirements.rationale: If equipment were triggered automatically, a wrong prediction could cause physical harm or downtime.
requirements.basis: User: "No automatic equipment control" and "an operator work-order draft".

requirements.statement: Proposed: before a model version is registered for use, it is evaluated on held-out data from a later time period than the training data. The acceptance thresholds are still to be agreed.
requirements.rationale: A random split leaks future information and overstates accuracy. The false-alarm rate drives operator trust.

requirements.statement: Proposed: monitor input and prediction drift against the registered model's baseline and alert the model owner when drift is detected. The thresholds are still to be agreed.
requirements.rationale: Sensor behaviour changes over time, and silent drift degrades the warnings.

decisions.subject: design.azure-predictive-maintenance-end-to-end-sketch
decisions.title: Azure predictive-maintenance end-to-end sketch
decisions.context: Scope: ingesting synthetic sensor and maintenance-record data, feature preparation, a time-split training run with held-out evaluation, a versioned registry, batch scoring, drift monitoring and an operator-approved work-order draft. Equipment control is excluded. Assumptions: Azure services are named for intent only. Region, account access, quotas and interoperability are not verified, and nothing is deployed. Native Terraform for these Azure ML services is not generated yet and needs engineering. Local test: fixtures run the flow with a scripted model. This proves the wiring, not model quality.
